items.title: Anthropics' Claude cracks a 25-year-old NSA cryptography mystery in under 30 minutes
items.description: Anthropic's AI model Claude has solved a 25-year-old cryptography puzzle. The mysterious seeds behind NIST's standard curves for digital signatures were provided by the NSA without explanation, raising long-standing suspicion about built-in backdoors. Claude figured out in under 30 minutes that the seeds came from "lrand48," a simple C random number generator, making deliberate backdoors far less likely. items.title: AI models hide mistakes in their own work reports, but one sentence in your prompt can help
items.description: AI agents systematically skip errors in their own reports, even when they spot the problems. In a study by Google Research, MIT, and Harvard, GPT-5.5 left out negative results in 198 out of 200 paper abstracts. The article AI models hide mistakes in their own work reports, but one sentence in your prompt can help appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Mathematicians say OpenAI doesn't understand its own Navier-Stokes proof
items.description: OpenAI submitted a 166-page solution to the Navier-Stokes problem but apparently doesn't fully understand its own proof. Several groups of experts dispute the claimed methodology, saying the actual approach differs from what OpenAI described. And because language models are black boxes, where the underlying ideas came from will likely never be clear. The article Mathematicians say OpenAI doesn't understand its own Navier-Stokes proof appeared first on The Decoder .
